correctness.rationale: Two exact partition reductions prove every mixed indicator moment; the covariance matrix is a rank-one constant part minus two permutation incidences. Fourier diagonalization and the verified Bell ratio inequality prove the exact gcd-based kernel and negative global covariance for every n>=3 and 1<=d<n. The standard-library checker corroborated with 4358 exact assertions through n=9 and Bell ratios through n=99; no finite enumeration is used to infer the universal result.

originality.rationale: The direct Callan and Munagi texts were inspected, and their aggregate equidistribution and marginal all-displacement enumerations were compared at the statement/implication level. Those statements do not supply the complete mixed local covariance matrix or its Fourier singular spectrum and arithmetic rank defect. The possibility of an implicit general theorem is retained as a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Historical priority cannot be established conclusively by literature search; a broader theorem on exchangeable random partitions or association-scheme incidences might imply the covariance matrix.

value.rationale: A natural equality of expected singleton and displacement-adjacency counts conceals an exact arithmetic rank transition and local/global sign reversal. The theorem gives a complete n,d classification and canonical nullspace basis, useful for understanding which linear contrasts of adjacency counts are uncorrelated with every singleton indicator, not just a table or arbitrary numerical example.
